*'''Squint''': Slang term commonly used by [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]]/[[New Republic/Legends|Republic]] pilots, in reference to the [[TIE/IN interceptor/Legends|TIE/IN interceptor]].<ref name="XRS" />
*'''SSD''': Abbreviation for [[Super Star Destroyer/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]].
*'''[[Stalbringion hells]]''': An expletive, e.g. "Where in eight [[Stalbringion hells]] did that come from?"<ref name="LSSM" />
*'''Stand-Back''': General term for [[Artillery/Legends|artillery]] crewers.<ref name="RB" />
*'''[[Stang/Legends|Stang]]''': An [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaanian]] swear word.<ref name="GTSWU1" /> Could also be used as an idiom to show that a person did not care about someone, such as, "Stang the kid anyway,"<ref name="BP">''[[The New Jedi Order: Balance Point]]''</ref> or as an adjective, e.g. "the stang thing."<ref name="Rogue Squadron 2">[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron 2|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' 2]]</ref> Similar to the real-world swear word "damn."
*'''Stanging''': Derogatory modifier, such as, "[[King/Legends|Queen]] of the stanging [[Sith/Legends|Sith]]."<ref name="Sacrifice" /> Similar to the real-world swear word "f*cking."
*'''[[Alliance Starbird|Starbirds]] in the Rafters''': [[Starfighter/Legends|Starfighters]] operating inside the [[Planetary shield/Legends|planetary shield]].<ref name="RB" />
*'''Star-forsaken''': An expression for an unideal location devoid of stars.<ref name="MJH" /> Similar to the real-world adjective "godforsaken."<ref name=":1" />
*'''Star-[[Gas/Legends|gas]]''': A curse apparently expressing doubt.<ref name="Hard Targets 4">[[Agent of the Empire – Hard Targets 4|''Agent of the Empire – Hard Targets'' 4]]</ref>
*'''Star-hopper''': Term for a spacer.<ref name="SW7" />
*'''Star jockey''': Term for a spacer.<ref name="ESB novel" />
*'''Star kitty''': According to [[Skids]], if you put too much ordnance on a [[BTL-S8 K-wing assault starfighter|K-wing]], you got a "mean-looking, chip-on-a-shoulder, fixing-for-trouble star kitty."<ref name="BTS" />
*'''Stars and [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxies]]!''': An exclamation.<ref name="Death of Hope">''[[Jedi Apprentice: The Death of Hope]]'' series</ref>
*'''Stars at night!''': An exclamation.<ref name="TBH:KK">''[[The Bounty Hunters: Kenix Kil]]''</ref>
*'''Stars and [[Planet/Legends|planets]]!''': An exclamation.<ref name="LOFJ">''[[Legacy of the Jedi]]''</ref>
*'''[[Stars' End/Legends|Stars' End]]''': A curse, referring to the penal colony located at one of the farthest ends of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] in the [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]].<ref name="LOE" />
*'''Starshine''': Used as a way of addressing someone.<ref name="Mara Jade 2">[[Mara Jade – By the Emperor's Hand 2|''Mara Jade – By the Emperor's Hand'' 2]]</ref> Similar to the real-world [[Wikipedia:British English|British English]] form of address "sunshine."<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.britannica.com/dictionary/sunshine|text=starshine|quote='''3''' ''British, informal'' — used as a form of address that can be either friendly or rude|work=''The [[Wikipedia:Encyclopædia Britannica|Britannica]] Dictionary''|archivedate=20230705004526}}</ref>
*'''Stars of Alderaan''': An exclamation.<ref name="VOTF" />
*'''Stars take your [[Color/Legends|black]] [[Bone/Legends|bones]]''': An expression of contempt toward another person.<ref name="Legacy 26" />
*'''[[Steel/Legends|Steel]]-[[Cat/Legends|kitten]]''': Narrator's description of [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia's]] tone of voice when she tries to convince [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] to kill her instead of allowing her to be taken alive by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], as seen in the novel ''[[Splinter of the Mind's Eye]]''.<ref name="SME" /> In the [[Star Wars: Splinter of the Mind's Eye (comic series)|comic adaptation]], Vader calls Leia a "steel kitten" during their [[duel on Mimban]].<ref name="Splinter 4">[[Splinter of the Mind's Eye 4|''Splinter of the Mind's Eye'' 4]]</ref>
*'''Step on the wrong Hutt's tail''': Non-[[canon]] term for doing something stupid.<ref name="Ghost" /> Similar to the real-world idiom "step on someone's toes," meaning to upset someone.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/step-on-toes|text=step on someone's toes|quote=to upset someone, esp. by getting involved in something that is that person's responsibility|work=[[Wikipedia:Cambridge University Press and Assessment|''Cambridge Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20230702202615}}</ref>
*'''Stick-in-the-[[Swamp/Legends|swamp]]''': A dull person who avoids trying new things.<ref name="Changing">''[[Jedi Quest: The Changing of the Guard]]''</ref> Similar to the real-world noun "stick-in-the-mud."<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/stick-in-the-mud|text=stick-in-the-mud|quote=someone who is old-fashioned and too serious and avoids enjoyable activities|work=[[Wikipedia:Cambridge University Press and Assessment|''Cambridge Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20221209041621}}</ref>
*'''Stinkweed''': An insult.<ref name="Life Below">{{CWACite|9|Life Below}}</ref>
*'''Stir up a [[Mynock/Legends|mynocks]]' nest''': To do something that causes trouble.<ref name="KOTOR2" /> Similar to the real-world idiom "stir up a hornet's nest."<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/stir-up-a-hornets-nest|text=stir up a hornet's nest|quote=to do something which causes a lot of controversy or produces a situation which is extremely difficult to deal with|work=[[Wikipedia:Collins English Dictionary|''Collins English Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20230420165416}}</ref>
*'''Stitch''': Slang for someone humorous, e.g. "You CorSec people are a stitch."<ref name="VOTF" /> Real world phrase.<ref name="Stitch">{{WebCite|url=https://idioms.thefreedictionary.com/a+stitch|text=a stitch|quote=Someone who is very humorous or amusing.|work=[[Wikipedia:The Free Dictionary|''The Free Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20210916183742}}</ref>
*'''Stop on a [[Decicred/Legends|dime]]''': To stop suddenly.<ref name="Star Wars: Starfighter">[[Star Wars: Starfighter (video game)|''Star Wars: Starfighter'']]</ref> Real-world idiom.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/stop-on-a-dime|text=stop on a dime|quote=to be able to stop almost immediately, even when moving very quickly|work=[[Wikipedia:Cambridge University Press and Assessment|''Cambridge Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20230603195121}}</ref>
*'''Stonemen''': Gallisport swoop gang slang for Imperial [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]].<ref name="SG" />
*'''Stoopa''': [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]] for "fool."<ref name="GPBTG" />
*'''Stopshort''': Elrood sector slang for the planet [[Torina]], which is one stop short of the end of the [[Elrood-Derilyn Trade Route]].<ref name="Planets Three" />
*'''Stormies''': A slang term for stormtroopers.<ref name="SWG:AED" />
*'''Street Cleaners''': Gallisport swoop gang slang for [[Imperial Army trooper/Legends|Imperial Army troopers]].<ref name="SG" />
*'''Strekkin'''': Used to express annoyance with someone, i.e. "strekkin' son of a [[Murglak/Legends|murglak]]…!" said by [[Gunn Yage]] about [[Cade Skywalker]].<ref name="Legacy 2006 39">[[Legacy (2006) 39|''Legacy'' (2006) 39]]</ref> Similar to the vulgar real-world swear word "f*cking."
*'''Stylishly dressed''': [[Gambler/Legends|Gambler]] slang for any being who appears to be unarmed. The opposite of '''nicely dressed'''.<ref name="CSWE" />
*'''SUBAR''': Gallisport swoop gang slang acronym for "Slagged Up Beyond All Repair."<ref name="SG" />
*'''Sucker''': Insult referring to someone easily deceived.<ref name="Coffin in the Clouds">[[Star Wars (1977) 56|''Star Wars'' (1977) 56]]</ref> Real-world noun.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/sucker|text=sucker|quote=a person who believes everything they are told and is therefore easy to deceive|work=[[Wikipedia:Cambridge University Press and Assessment|''Cambridge Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20230617183833}}</ref>
*'''Sucks void''': Expression describing circumstances as welcome as a pressure leak.<ref name="Legacy 4" />
*'''Suffering satellites''': An exclamation of anger.<ref name="D:TLP">{{DroidsCite|The Lost Prince}}</ref>
*'''Suffering Sullorians''': An exclamation of impatience.<ref name="TBH:SW" />
*'''Suicide Sled''': A colloquial term used by [[Starfighter/Legends|fighter]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] to describe the [[Z-95 Headhunter/Legends|Z-95 Headhunter]].<ref name="HSSE" />
*'''Sunbather''': Alliance SpecOp term for an [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]] agent.<ref name="CSWE" />
*'''Sun bonnet''': Clone trooper helmet.<ref name="Rookies" />
*'''Sun-scorched ball''': Mos Eisley slang for Tatooine.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 7" />
*'''Superior Model''': Clone trooper for Clone Commando.
*'''Super Star Destroyer''': A warship larger and/or more powerful than a Star Destroyer but similar in shape.<ref name="ITW:SWT">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]''</ref>
*'''Swarm of [[Gnat/Legends|gnats]]''': Elrood sector slang for [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter|TIE fighters]].<ref name="Planets Three" />
*'''Sweet mother of [[Chaos/Legends|chaos]]''': An exclamation<ref name="BTS" /> similar to the real-world exclamation "sweet Mary, mother of God/Jesus."<ref name="Sweet Mary">{{WebCite|url=https://idioms.thefreedictionary.com/sweet+Mary(%2c+mother+of+God)|text=sweet Mary(, <small>''[sic]''</small> mother of God)|quote=An exclamation of alarm, amazement, or exasperation.|work=[[Wikipedia:The Free Dictionary|''The Free Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20250307201418}}</ref><ref>{{WebCite|url=https://idioms.thefreedictionary.com/sweet+Mary%2c+mother+of+Jesus|text=sweet Mary, mother of Jesus|quote=An exclamation of alarm, amazement, or exasperation.|work=[[Wikipedia:The Free Dictionary|''The Free Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20250313232133}}</ref>
*'''Sweet Queen Quinella''': An exclamation.<ref name="DS" /> Similar to the real-world exclamation "sweet Mary."<ref name="Sweet Mary" />
*'''Sweet Sookie''': An exclamation.<ref name="MBS" /><ref name="Coruscant Nights II">''[[Coruscant Nights II: Street of Shadows]]''</ref> Similar to the real-world exclamation "sweet Mary."<ref name="Sweet Mary" />
*'''Sweet soalie!''': An exclamation.<ref name="MBS" /> Similar to the real-world exclamation "sweet Mary."<ref name="Sweet Mary" />
*'''Switch off!''': An exclamation used among droids corresponding to "sod off!" or "shut up!"<ref name="ESB" />
*'''Swooper''': Gallisport swoop gang slang for a swoop gang member.<ref name="SG" />
*'''Swoopie''': A member of a [[swoop]]-bike gang.<ref name="Union 2">[[Union 2|''Union'' 2]]</ref>

==T==
*'''[[Tabaga-and-Vrelt]]''': A type of game.<ref name="THG" /> Similar to the real-world noun "cat and mouse," a type of behavior akin to that of a cat playing with its prey, such as toying with or tormenting someone before killing them, or an intricate game involving endless pursuit, almost getting caught and narrowly escaping.<ref name="Catnap" />
*'''Tailhead''': Slang for [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'leks]].<ref name="Innocents">{{TCW|Innocents of Ryloth}}</ref>
*'''Tall-dark-and-ugly-as-sin''': Used by [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] to address [[Warto]].<ref name="SW8" /> A parody of the real-world phrase "tall, dark and handsome", a cliché used to describe the archetypal attributes of an attractive man, often embodied in the protagonists of romance books and movies.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://idioms.thefreedictionary.com/tall%2C+dark+and+handsome|text=tall, dark, and handsome|quote=''cliché'' The stereotypical traits of an attractive man, as are often found in the heroes of romance novels and films.|work=[[Wikipedia:The Free Dictionary|''The Free Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20230509103836}}</ref>
*'''Taken up [[Mining/Legends|mining]]''': [[Elrood sector/Legends|Elrood sector]] slang for an unlucky person who was caught by the Empire while trying to complete the [[Elrood-Derilyn Trade Route]].<ref name="Planets Three" />
*'''TAM''': Threatening Armored Man. SpecOps term for an armored [[Storm commando/Legends|Imperial Storm Commando]].<ref name="GG9" />
*'''Target''': [[Pilot/Legends|Pilot]] and [[Gunner/Legends|gunner]] term for armored vehicles. Heavy [[Tank/Legends|tank]] are "slow targets," [[All Terrain Armored Transport|AT-ATs]] are "slow easy targets," [[Speeder/Legends|speeders]] or light tanks are "fast targets."<ref name="RB" />
*'''[[Tarhead]]''': An insectoid addicted to [[Membrosia/Legends|black membrosia]].<ref name="The Swarm War" />
*'''[[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Tarkin's]] [[Tooth/Legends|Teeth]]''': An [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] exclamation, after [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Tarkin's]] death.<ref name="VOTF" />
*'''[[Tarrek's eyes!]]''': Exclamatory phrase used by the [[Velabri (species)|Velabri]] [[Quillin Arkell]].<ref name="SF">{{Journal|12|Small Favors}}</ref>
*'''Tatoo''': In [[Mos Eisley]], the Imperial reference for [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine's]] [[Binary star/Legends|twin suns]], [[Tatoo I/Legends|Tatoo I]] and [[Tatoo II/Legends|Tatoo II]].<ref name="Galaxy Guide 7" />
*'''TCTL''': Elrood sector acronym for "too cute to live."<ref name="Planets Three" />
*'''Tee-my''' or '''TMAI''': "Throw [[Currency/Legends|Money]] At It"; slang used by builders and [[Technician/Legends|mechanics]].<ref name="DS" />
*'''Thank the [[Maker/Legends|Maker]]!''': An expression of relief. Used by [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] to refer to his creator, rather than an organic referring to a deity.<ref name="ANH" /> Similar to the real-world idiom "thank God."<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/thank-god|text=thank God|quote=something you say when you are happy because something bad did not happen:|work=[[Wikipedia:Cambridge University Press and Assessment|''Cambridge Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20210725073717}}</ref>
*'''Thank the [[Star/Legends|stars]]''': An expression of relief.<ref name="Crimson Empire II 3">[[Crimson Empire II: Council of Blood 3|''Crimson Empire II: Council of Blood'' 3]]</ref><ref name="Showdown at Centerpoint">''[[Showdown at Centerpoint]]''</ref> Real-world interjection.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.wordhippo.com/what-is/another-word-for/thank_the_stars.html|text=thank the stars|quote='''Interjection''' Used to express gratitude or relief that something is the case '''Adverb''' In a fortunate manner |work=WordHippo|archivedate=20250707224257}}</ref>
*'''The Big Isn't''': A phrase used by [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] in reference to space.<ref name="BFTFTS">''[[Boba Fett: The Fight to Survive]]''</ref>
*'''The Entropy I can't''': An expletive.<ref name="LCMS" />
*'''There'll be [[Chaos/Legends|hell]] to pay''': Used to emphasize that there will be serious trouble.<ref name="ANH" /> Real world idiom.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/there-ll-be-hell-to-pay|text=there'll be hell to pay|quote=something you say that means someone will be very angry if something happens|work=[[Wikipedia:Cambridge University Press and Assessment|''Cambridge Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20201102112754}}</ref>
*'''There's more than one way to skin a [[Womp rat/Legends|womp rat]]''': Meaning that there is more than one way to achieve an aim.<ref name="Mystery">{{TCW|Mystery of a Thousand Moons}}</ref> Similar to the real world saying "there's more than one way to skin a cat."<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/theres-more-than-one-way-to-skin-a-cat|text=there's more than one way to skin a cat|quote=there are several ways to achieve something|work=[[Wikipedia:Collins English Dictionary|''Collins English Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20221221060252}}</ref>
*'''Those who wish to rid themselves of [[fleeg]]s must clean the hair of their neighbors''': [[Askajian/Legends|Askajian]] saying.<ref name="TG" />
*'''Throw a huge [[Hydrospanner/Legends|hydrospanner]] in the works''': To do something that keeps a plan or activity from succeeding.<ref name="RC:TC" /> Similar to the real-world British phrase "put/throw a spanner in the works."<ref name="Spanner">{{WebCite|url=https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/put-throw-a-spanner-in-the-works|text=put/throw a spanner in the works|quote='''''idiom''''' UK (US '''throw a (monkey) wrench in the works''') to do something that prevents a plan or activity from succeedings|work=[[Wikipedia:Cambridge University Press and Assessment|''Cambridge Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20230307055508}}</ref>
*'''Throw a hydrospanner into someone's plans''': To do something that keeps someone's plans from succeeding.<ref name="Tempest" /> Similar to the real-world British phrase "put/throw a spanner in the works."<ref name="Spanner" />
*'''Throwing a bent hydrospanner into someone's talks''': To do something to keep someone's talks from succeeding.<ref name="Darksaber">[[Darksaber (novel)|''Darksaber'']]</ref> Similar to the real-world British phrase "put/throw a spanner in the works."<ref name="Spanner" />
*'''Ticktils''': Elrood sector slang for cute species such as [[Bilar]]s. A pronunciation of '''TCTL''', an acronym for "too cute to live."<ref name="Planets Three" />
*'''Tie a [[Rope/Legends|noose]] around someone's neck''': To trap someone in a difficult situation.<ref name="Star Wars (1977) 30">[[Star Wars (1977) 30|''Star Wars'' (1977) 30]]</ref> "A noose around someone's neck" is a real-world metaphor.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/noose|text=noose|quote=You can refer to something that traps people in a difficult situation as a noose around their neck.|work=[[Wikipedia:Collins English Dictionary|''Collins English Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20230303171453}}</ref>
*'''Tinfish Bucket''': [[Alliance Special Operations/Legends|SpecOps]] term for an Imperial [[Aquatic Terrain Armored Transport|AT-AT swimmer]].<ref name="GG9" />
*'''[[Tinnie/Legends|Tinnies''']]: Slang for droids. Commonly used by the [[Omega Squad]] members and [[Clone commando/Legends|clone commandos]] trained by [[Walon Vau]].<ref name="RC:HC" />
*'''Tiny Tanks''': Tanker crew term for [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]].<ref name="RB" />
*'''TK''': Short for telekinesis.<ref name="DT1" />
*'''TLA''': Three-Letter Acronym. An '''ETLA''' is an Extended Three-Letter Acronym; that is, a four-letter acronym.<ref name="GG9" />
*'''To Tatooine with''': Used to say that the speaker not care about something, e.g. "To Tatooine with the economic conoditions here!"<ref name="GG6" /> Similar to the real-world idiom "to hell with someone/something."<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/to-hell-with|text=to hell with someone/something|quote=used to say that you do not care about someone or something|work=[[Wikipedia:Cambridge University Press and Assessment|''Cambridge Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20230625165110}}</ref>
*'''To Vader with''': A phrase followed by a subject the speaker does not particularly care for, e.g. "...to Vader with these preliminaries."<ref name="Specter of the Past" /> Its meaning was similar to the real-world phrase "to hell with".
*'''Toaster''': [[Gallisport]] [[Swoop gang/Legends|swoop gang]] slang. A [[Thermal detonator/Legends|thermal detonator]].<ref name="SG" />
*'''Toots''': A slang term [[Jaxxon/Legends|Jaxxon]] used to address women such as [[Amaiza Foxtrain/Legends|Amaiza Foxtrain]].<ref name="SW10" />
*'''Torch''': [[Gallisport]] [[Swoop gang/Legends|swoop gang]] slang. A [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]].<ref name="SG" />
*'''Torp''': Slang for a torpedo, usually [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedoes]] or [[flechette torpedo]]es.<ref name="LSSM" />
*'''Touch a circuit''': To upset someone, more specifically a [[Droid/Legends|droid]].<ref name="Medstar II">''[[MedStar II: Jedi Healer]]''</ref> Similar to the real-world idiom "touch a nerve."<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/hit-touch-a-raw-nerve|text=hit/touch a (raw) nerve|quote=to upset someone|work=[[Wikipedia:Cambridge University Press and Assessment|''Cambridge Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20241208071000}}</ref>
*'''Tough as a septoid''': Very resilient, hard to kill, like the seven-legged [[Septoid/Legends|septoid]] ([[Eriadu/Legends|Eriaduan]] phrase).<ref name="GatORW" />
*'''Tourist''': Mos Eisley slang for a person unable to get anything done. Name actually refers to [[Governor/Legends|Governor]] [[Tour Aryon|Tour Aryon's]] widely regarded inability to accomplish anything, i.e., "Tour-ist." Deliberately confusing to visitors.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 7" />
*'''Toxic''': [[Alliance Intelligence/Legends|Alliance Intelligence]] slang for infiltrated by [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence]] [[Agent/Legends|agents]].<ref name="Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" />
*'''[[Toz]]''': Elrood sector word for a grain plant grown on [[Merisee/Legends|Merisee]].<ref name="Planets Three" />
*'''Tozzed''': Elrood sector slang for drunk; seemingly referring to toz, a grain plant brewed into an alcoholic beverage called [[utoz]].<ref name="Planets Three" />
*'''Tracers''': Elrood sector slang for bounty hunters.<ref name="Planets Three" />
*'''Treadfoot''': General armored crew slang for infantry.<ref name="RB" />
*'''[[Trench Run Defense|Trench Run disease]]''': A weakness that all capital cruisers had.<ref name="XRS" />
*'''Triage code X''': Too badly injured; not expected to survive despite medical attention.<ref name="RC:TZ" />
*'''Trip''': Slang term commonly used by [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]]/[[New Republic/Legends|Republic]] pilots, in reference to the [[TIE/d "Defender" Multi-Role Starfighter/Legends|TIE Defender]].<ref name="XIR" />
*'''Triple-A''': Slang term used by [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] to refer to anti-aircraft artillery.<ref name="CSWE" />
*'''Triple tap''': Military term for the firing of three blaster bolts in quick succession.<ref name="CSWE" />
*'''Triple Zero''': Military slang for [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], due to its hyperspace coordinates.<ref name="Galaxy at War" /><ref name="RC:TZ" />
*'''Trollop''': An insult.<ref name="Tempest" /> Real-world [[Wikipedia:British English|British English]] derogatory word for a promiscuous or untidy woman.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/trollop|text=Trollop|quote='''in British English''' ''NOUN derogatory'' '''1.''' a promiscuous woman '''2.''' an untidy woman; slattern|work=[[Wikipedia:Collins English Dictionary|''Collins English Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20230427212822}}</ref>
*'''Tron''': SpecOps term for causing an opposing vehicle to crash spectacularly. ("That's tronned it.")<ref name="GG9" />
*'''Tub of [[Bantha/Legends|bantha]] fat''': A fat being.<ref name="JQTDG" />
*'''Tsan murra''': A [[Ysannan/Legends|Ysannan]] curse.<ref name="Empire's End 1" />
*'''Tsup''': A [[Yuuzhan Vong]] insult, translating loosely as "wicked slave."<ref name="EOV2:R">''[[The New Jedi Order: Edge of Victory II: Rebirth]]''</ref>
*'''Tumble''': To trace back to someone or something, e.g., "...tumbling to you means they've also tumbled to me..."<ref name="VOTF" />
*'''[[Tusker]] poop''': A [[Korun/Legends|Korun]] term for nonsense, or something of bad quality. See also '''not give a bucket of tusker poop'''.<ref name="SP" /> Similar to the real-world vulgar noun "bullshit."
*'''Tweezer''': A reference to the [[BX-series droid commando/Legends|BX-series droid commando]] made by either Captain Rex or Commander Cody.<ref name="Rookies" />
*'''Twit''': An insult.<ref name="ROTJ" /> Real-world word, meaning a stupid person.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/dictionary/english/twit|text=twit|quote=a stupid person|work=[[Wikipedia:Cambridge University Press and Assessment|''Cambridge Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20221025184728}}</ref>
*'''Two-[[Limb/Legends|toed]] [[Swamp/Legends|swamp]]-sucker''': An insult.<ref name="The White Witch" /> Similar to the real-world noun "egg-sucker."<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://idioms.thefreedictionary.com/egg-sucker|text=egg-sucker|quote=Someone who seeks out the approval, attention, and/or support of others, especially superiors, through abject subservience, flattery, or fawning.|work=[[Wikipedia:The Free Dictionary|''The Free Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20230208233523}}</ref>

==U==
*'''U.C.T.''' or '''universal Cutting Tool''': [[Lightsaber/Legends|Lightsaber]].<ref name="GG9" /><ref name="SQ" />
*'''[[Ugly/Legends|Ugly]]''': Term for a [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] made from parts of varying origins.<ref name="AAC" />
*'''Ugnor's Thumbs''': A mild expletive used by the [[Ugnaught/Legends|Ugnaughts]] who lived and worked on [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]].<ref name="Bespin Action">{{WizardsCite|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20041021bespin4|text=Bespin: Action Tidings, Part 4: The Empire's Ugly Nose}}</ref>
*'''[[Unluckies]]''': [[Elrood sector/Legends|Elrood sector]] slang for visitors to the sector.<ref name="Planets Three" />
*'''Uptown''': Citizen of the [[Upper City]] of [[Taris/Legends|Taris]].<ref name="kotor3">[[Knights of the Old Republic 3|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 3]]</ref>
*'''Utinni''': Exclamation made by various [[Jawa/Legends|Jawas]].<ref name="ANH" />
*'''[[Utoz]]''': Elrood sector name of a popular drink brewed from [[toz]] grain.<ref name="Planets Three" />
*'''[[Utozz]]''': Elrood sector name of a brand of '''Utoz'''.<ref name="Planets Three" />

==V==
*'''Vaccinate''': [[Alliance Intelligence/Legends|Alliance Intelligence]] slang for removing known [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Agent/Legends|agents]].<ref name="Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /> Also [[deal-slang]] for insuring or preventing a deal from falling apart.<ref name="Gambler's Life" />
*'''Vac-head''': An insult.<ref name="Crucible" />
*'''Vacuum''': Alliance Intelligence slang for deep undercover.<ref name="Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" />
*'''Vader-ripped''': A modifier.<ref name="VOTF" />
*'''Vader knows''': Emphasis that the speaker does not know something.<ref name="VOTF" /> Similar to the real-world phrase "God knows".
*'''Vader take''': See '''to Vader with'''.<ref name="VOTF" />
*'''[[Vader's eyes]]''': An exclamation.<ref name="TTAS">{{StoryCite|story=Tilotny Throws a Shape|book=The Empire Strikes Back Monthly 154|bformatted=''The Empire Strikes Back Monthly'' 154}}</ref>
*'''Vair's eyelids''': An exclamation.<ref name="Stock" />
*'''Vape''' or '''vap''': Short for "vaporize." [[Starfighter/Legends|Starfighter]] pilot slang for destroying a target, especially in a dogfight.<ref name="XRS" />
*'''Vapebait''': An unskilled pilot who makes an easy target.<ref name="XW">[[Star Wars: X-Wing (novel series)|''X-Wing'']]</ref>
*'''Vapin{{'}}''': A modifier.<ref name="DJ" />
*'''Vaping Moffs!''': An exclamation.<ref name="EOV2:R" />
*'''Vench my skug''': Exclamation of surprise,<ref name="Nampi" /><ref name="Podracing Tales">"[[Podracing Tales]]"</ref> most likely [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]] in origin.<ref name="Cuss" />
*'''Verre d'n Nocka!''': A [[Kerestian/Legends|Kerestian]] curse.<ref name="SSR">''[[Secrets of the Sisar Run]]''</ref>
*'''Verre!''': A short version of '''Verre d'n Nocka'''!<ref name="SSR" />
*'''[[Vhlor]]''': [[Yuuzhan Vong]] word used as an insult, it is the name of a filthy Yuuzhan Vong animal.<ref name="EOV2:R" />
*'''Victim''': A slang word that [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] used in reference to a [[Victory-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Victory''-class Star Destroyer]].<ref name="CSWE" />
*'''Vidlink''': A short version of "video link."<ref name="TIA">{{StoryCite|story=Therefore I Am: The Tale of IG-88|book=Tales of the Bounty Hunters}}</ref>
*'''Viper''': A treacherous person.<ref name="Rogue Squadron 29" /> Real-world literary noun.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/viper|text=viper|quote=<small>''literary</small> a very unpleasant person who you cannot trust|work=[[Wikipedia:Cambridge University Press and Assessment|''Cambridge Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20230624164511}}</ref>
*'''Vong''': Incorrect abbreviation for the Yuuzhan Vong which implied sacrilege and insult.<ref name="Conquest" />
*'''Vos''': Expletive used by [[Tycho Celchu/Legends|Tycho Celchu]].<ref name="Rogue Squadron 3" />

==W==
*'''Walker''': Term used by the winged [[S'kytri]] [[species]] for individuals who were incapable of flying.<ref name="SkyeWalkers" />
*'''Walking carpet''': Derogatory term [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] once applied to [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], referring to his shaggy coat.<ref name="ANH" />
*'''Wake-up call''': [[Alliance Special Operations/Legends|SpecOps]] term for a [[Grenade/Legends|grenade]].<ref name="GG9" />
*'''Wannabies''': Repulsor-crew term for [[hovercraft]].<ref name="RB" />
*'''War ain't a talent show''': A phrase attributed to [[Garbelian]], who spoke it at [[Averam/Legends|Averam]]. [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] [[Jarrow Rusher]] said this to encourage a [[Beadle Lubboon|clumsy recruit]] in the [[Rusher's Brigade]].<ref name="Knight Errant novel" />
*'''Warp-lagged''': A phrase referring to a feeling of tiredness after traveling in [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]].<ref name="BFTFTS" /> Similar to the real-world adjective "jet-lagged."<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/jet-lagged|text=jet-lagged|quote=tired and confused because you have made a long trip by plane from a place where the time is different|work=[[Wikipedia:Cambridge University Press and Assessment|''Cambridge Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20230424005248}}</ref>
*'''Wash out''': Term for a person who failed to make a certain cut. Jedi [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Tyzen Xebec]] used the term for [[Agricultural Corps/Legends|Agricultural Corps]] member [[Sanya]] when the pair met on first met on [[Ukio/Legends|Ukio]].
*'''Waste of good genes''': A phrase among the [[Cloning/Legends|clones]] of the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] referring to incompetence of a fellow clone.<ref name="SWRC" />
*'''[[Water/Legends|Water]] mixes with water''': A [[Dantari]] saying referring to a problem that can't be solved.<ref name="GOF:C">''[[Galaxy of Fear: Clones]]''</ref>
*'''Well, I'll be!''': Exclamation used to express astonishment.<ref name="CWMIA" /> Real-world expression.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://idioms.thefreedictionary.com/well+I%27ll+be|text=(well,) I'll be!|quote=An expression of surprise or astonishment, especially regarding some recent revelation.|work=[[Wikipedia:The Free Dictionary|''The Free Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20230526133539}}</ref>
*'''Wet''': A term used by [[Republic Commando]]s to designate non-[[droid]] targets.<ref name="RC:HC" />
*'''Wet-dock''': [[Elrood sector/Legends|Elrood sector]] slang term for a [[Cantina/Legends|bar]].<ref name="Planets Three" />
*'''[[Wet Droids]]''': A derogatory term for [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] and [[Clone commando/Legends|clone commandos]].<ref name="RC:HC" />
*'''Whatever the [[frizz]]''': Used as an intensifier.<ref name="OF" /> "Frizz" is similar to the real-world slang word "frick," a euphemism for the offensive swear word "f*ck".<ref name="Frick" />
*'''Whatever the [[Kriff/Legends|kriff]]''': Used as an intensifier, e.g. "whatever the kriff was happening to him."<ref name="Wild Space">''[[The Clone Wars: Wild Space]]''</ref> Since "kriff" is believed to be the ''Star Wars'' version of the swear word "f*ck,"<ref name="SW.com" /> "whatever the kriff" would be similar to the real-world offensive phrases "whatever the f*ck."
*'''Whatever the [[Stang/Legends|stang]]''': Used as an intensifier, e.g. "Whatever the stang her paymaster called itself."<ref name="Sacrifice" /> Similar to the real-world phrase "whatever the hell."
*'''What in all [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]&hellip;''': Expression used to express shock or surprise.<ref name="Jedi Search" /> Similar to the real-world phrase "what in the world&hellip;"
*'''What in blazes&hellip;''' or '''what in the blue blazes&hellip;''': Both an exclamation<ref name="DJ" /> and an intensifier<ref name="Specter of the Past" /> from the real world.<ref name="Blue blazes">{{WebCite|url=https://idioms.thefreedictionary.com/what+the+blue+blazes|text=what the (blue) blazes|quote=An exclamation used to emphasize surprise, shock, anger, disgust, etc. In this phrase, "the blazes" is used as an intensifier. The phrase can also be used with other question words (e.g. "who," "why," "how," etc.).|work=[[Wikipedia:The Free Dictionary|''The Free Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20230424205659}}</ref>
*'''What in the&hellip;''': Exclamation of surprise.<ref name="TFP" /><ref name="Heist">{{InsiderCite|138|Heist|reprint=1}}</ref> Similar to the real-world phrase "what in the world&hellip;"
*'''What in [[Galactic Empire/Legends|the Empire]]&hellip;''': Both an exclamation and an intensifier,<ref name="Specter of the Past" /><ref name="Heir to the Empire" /> e.g. "What in the Empire are [[Vilim Disra|you]] so afraid of, anyway?"<ref name="Specter of the Past" /> Similar to the real-world phrase "what in the world&hellip;"
*'''What in the eternal blue blazes&hellip;''': An exclamation.<ref name="LCMS" /> Variant of the real-world exclamation "what in the blue blazes."<ref name="Blue blazes" />
*'''What in the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]&hellip;''': Expression used to express shock or surprise.<ref name="The Last Command">''[[The Last Command]]''</ref> Similar to the real-world phrase "what in the world&hellip;"
*'''What in the name of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] dust''': Used to add emphasis to a question.<ref name="VOTF" /> Similar to the real-world phrase "what in the name of heaven."<ref name="In the name of heaven">{{WebCite|url=https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/in-the-name-of-someone-in-the-name-of-something|text=in the name of sb/in the name of sth|quote=People sometimes use expressions such as 'in the name of heaven' or 'in the name of humanity' to add emphasis to a question or request. ''[emphasis] What in the name of heaven's going on?''|work=[[Wikipedia:Collins English Dictionary|''Collins English Dictionary'']]|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/GcRxJ}}</ref>
*'''What in the name of blazes&hellip;''': Used to express shock or surprise.<ref name="The Hutt Gambit">''[[The Hutt Gambit]]''</ref> Similar to the real-world exclamations "what in the blue blazes"<ref name="Blue blazes" /> and "what in the name of heaven."<ref name="In the name of heaven" />
*'''What in the name of the Edge, the Core, and everything in between&hellip;''': Used to express shock or surprise.<ref name="LCSTB" /> Similar to the real-world phrase "what in the name of heaven."<ref name="In the name of heaven" />
*'''What in the name of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]''': Used to add emphasis to a question.<ref name="VOTF" /> Similar to the real-world phrase "what in the name of heaven."<ref name="In the name of heaven" />
*'''What in the name of the Original Light''': Used as a mild oath, perhaps pertaining to creation.<ref name="HSSE" /><ref name="HSRevenge" /> Similar to the real-world phrase "what in the name of heaven."<ref name="In the name of heaven" />
*'''What in the [[Universe/Legends|universe]]&hellip;''': Expression used to express shock or surprise, e.g. "What in the universe was that?"<ref name="Overlords">{{TCW|Overlords}}</ref> Similar to the real-world phrase "what in the world&hellip;"
*'''What in the [[Planet/Legends|worlds]]&hellip;''' Expression used to express shock or surprise.<ref name="SQ" /> Similar to the real-world phrase "what in the world&hellip;"
*'''What in space&hellip;''': An exclamation of surprise.<ref name="Specter of the Past" /> Similar to the real-world phrase "what in the world&hellip;".
*'''What on nine ice worlds&hellip;''': An exclamation.<ref name="Mercy Kill">''[[X-Wing: Mercy Kill]]''</ref> Similar to the real-world idiom "what on earth."<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/what-on-earth|text=what on earth|quote=used for showing surprise|work=[[Wikipedia:Cambridge University Press and Assessment|''Cambridge Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20230525225059}}</ref>
*'''What's the trouble?''': Elrood sector slang term, meaning "What's the price?".<ref name="Planets Three" />
*'''What's your beef?''': Used by [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] when being threatened by [[Warto]].<ref name="SW8" /> Real-world phrase.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://idioms.thefreedictionary.com/what%27s+your+beef|text=What's (one's) beef (with someone or something)?|quote=Why is one upset (with someone or something)? What is one's problem (with someone or something)?|archivedate=20230603185301}}</ref>
*'''What the&hellip;''': Exclamation<ref name="AOTC" /> from the real world.
*'''What the [[bloah]]''': An interjection, e.g. "What the bloah is that?"<ref name="The Joiner King" /> Similar to the real-world phrase "what the hell."
*'''What the [[chubba]]''': An interjection, e.g. "What the chubba is going on!".<ref name="The Unseen Queen" /> Similar to the real-world phrase "what the hell."
*'''What the deuce''': An exclamation<ref name="LCMS" /> from the real world, with "deuce" being a minced oath for "devil".<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://idioms.thefreedictionary.com/What+the+deuce%3F|text=what the deuce?|quote=An exclamation used to emphasize surprise, shock, or bafflement. ("Deuce" is a minced oath used instead of the word "devil.")|work=[[Wikipedia:The Free Dictionary|''The Free Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20230525223518}}</ref>
*'''What the fracas''': An interjection, e.g. "What the fracas are you doing?"<ref name="VOTF" /> Similar to the real-world phrase "what the f*ck."
*'''What the frotz''': Exclamation used to express anger.<ref name="Hapes 2" /> Similar to the real-world vulgar slang phrase "what the f*ck."
*'''What the [[Chaos/Legends|hell]]''': Phrase used to express anger.<ref name="ANH" /><ref name="Rookies" /> Real-world exclamation.
*'''What the kriff''': Used as an intensifier, e.g. "What the kriff are you--"<ref name="KE1">[[Knight Errant: Aflame 1|''Knight Errant: Aflame'' 1]]</ref> Since "kriff" is believed to be the ''Star Wars'' version of the swear word "f*ck,"<ref name="SW.com" /> "what the kriff" would be similar to the real-world offensive phrase "what the f*ck."
*'''What the stang''': Used as an intensifier, e.g. "What the stang have you ''done'' to me?".<ref name="Sacrifice" /> Similar to the real-world phrase "what the hell."
*'''What the stinkin' stang''': Used as an intensifier, e.g. "What the stinkin' stang's goin' on."<ref name="POT" /> Similar to the real-world phrase "what the bloody hell."
*'''What the varp''': Used as an intensifier, e.g. "''Perhaps?'' What the varp do [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|you]] mean, ''perhaps''?"<ref name="Wild Space" /> Similar to the real-world phrase "what the hell."
*'''What/where in the blazes&hellip;''': An exclamation of surprise at a spectacle or event.<ref name="SW8" /><ref name="AOTC" /> Real-world exclamation.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://idioms.thefreedictionary.com/what+in+the+blazes|text=in (the) blazes?|quote=Used as an intensifier after a question word (who, what, where, when, why, and how) to express extreme confusion, surprise, or aggravation. Primarily heard in US.|work=[[Wikipedia:The Free Dictionary|''The Free Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20230423195022}}</ref>
*'''What/why the frizz''': Used as an intensifier.<ref name="DL" /> "Frizz" is similar to the real-world slang word "frick," a euphemism for the offensive swear word "f*ck."<ref name="Frick" />
*'''When [[Bantha/Legends|banthas]] fly''': Non-[[canon]] phrase meaning "extremely unlikely."<ref name="Force Fiction">{{Tales|7|Force Fiction}}</ref> Similar to the real-world phrase "when pigs fly."<ref name="Fly little piggy">{{WebCite|url=https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/when-pigs-fly|text=when pigs fly|quote=If you say `when pigs fly' after someone has said that something might happen, you are emphasizing that you think it is very unlikely.|work=[[Wikipedia:Collins English Dictionary|''Collins English Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20210507001157}}</ref>
*'''When [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]] ride [[Swoop/Legends|swoops]]!''': Extremely unlikely.<ref name="The Unseen Queen" /> Similar to the real-world phrase "when pigs fly."<ref name="Fly little piggy" />
*'''When [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]] freezes over''': Extremely unlikely.<ref name="RC:HC" /> Similar to the real-world idiom "when hell freezes over."<ref name="Hell freeze">{{WebCite|url=https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/when-hell-freezes-over|text=when hell freezes over|quote=If you say that something will happen when hell freezes over, you mean that it will never happen.|work=[[Wikipedia:Cambridge University Press and Assessment|''Cambridge Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20210506215355}}</ref>
*'''When it snows on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]!''': Extremely unlikely to happen.<ref name="ROTS Jr."> [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (junior novelization)|''Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith'' junior novelization]]</ref> Similar to the real-world idiom "when hell freezes over."<ref name="Hell freeze" />
*'''When [[Jawa/Legends|Jawas]] swim!''': Extremely unlikely.<ref name="Star by Star" /> Similar to the real-world phrase "when pigs fly."<ref name="Fly little piggy" />
*'''When [[Plebo/Legends|plebos]] fly out of my hump''': Phrase used by [[Mama/Legends|Mama the Hutt]] to indicate that something would never happen.<ref name="Hunt for Ziro" /> Similar to the real-world phrase "when pigs fly."<ref name="Fly little piggy" />
*'''When [[Sarlacc/Legends|sarlaccs]] fly!''': Extremely unlikely.<ref name="The Unseen Queen" /> Similar to the real-world phrase "when pigs fly."<ref name="Fly little piggy" />
*'''Where the stang''': Used as an intensifier, e.g. "Where the stang was [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Kenobi]]?"<ref name="TCW novel" />
*'''[[Color/Legends|White]] [[Armor]]''': Armor crew slang for [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]].<ref name="RB" />
*'''White-hats''': Slang for Imperial stormtroopers.<ref name="HSLL" />
*'''Whingeing jimmies''': Slang for being frightened. "It gives me the whingeing jimmies."<ref name="LSSM" />
*'''White [[Elephant/Legends|elephant]]''': A term for something that costs more to maintain than it's worth.<ref name="LCMS" />
*'''White job''': Slang for [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone trooper]].<ref name="RC:TZ" />
*'''White wonders''': Elrood sector derisive slang term for stormtroopers.<ref name="Planets Three" />
*'''Who in blazes...''': Both an explanation and an intensifier<ref name="VOTF" /> from the real world.<ref name="Blue blazes" />
*'''Who pissed in ''your'' power supply?''': Roughly translates to "Who pissed ''you'' off?" Said mainly to droids.<ref name="DM:SH" /> Similar to real-world rude slang terms such as "piss in (one's) cereal," "piss on (someone's) chips" etc.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://idioms.thefreedictionary.com/piss+in+your+cereal|text=piss in (one's) cereal|quote=''rude slang'' To upset, irritate, or disappoint one, especially to an extreme or excessive degree. (…) See also: piss in (one's) food • piss in (one's) soup • piss on (someone's) chips • piss on (someone's) bonfire • piss in (someone's) Corn Flakes • piss in (someone's) Cheerios (…) shit in (one's) Cheerios|work=[[Wikipedia:The Free Dictionary|''The Free Dictionary'']]|archiveurl=https://archive.is/oarHK}}</ref>
*'''Who the stang''': Used as an intensifier, e.g. "Who the stang are you?"<ref name="O66" /> Similar to the real-world phrase "who the hell."
*'''[[Wild bantha chase/Legends|Wild bantha chase]]''' or '''wild bantha hunt''': A futile search.<ref name="ROTS" /><ref name="Ruins of Dantooine">''[[Star Wars Galaxies: The Ruins of Dantooine]]''</ref> Similar to the real-world phrase "wild goose chase."<ref name="Goosey">{{WebCite|url=https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/wild-goose-chase|text=wild goose chase|quote='a search for something that is impossible for you to find or that does not exist, that makes you waste a lot of time|work=[[Wikipedia:Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary|''Oxford Learner's Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20260121163924}}</ref>
*'''Wild [[Caranak/Legends|caranak]] chase''': See '''wild bantha chase'''.<ref name="Ascension" />
*'''[[Wild goose]]''': When [[Javis Tyrr]] was sent on a fruitless search at the [[Indigo Tower]], [[Tahiri Veila]] referred to the operation as a "wild goose."<ref name="Omen">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Omen]]''</ref> An abbreviated version of the real-world idiom "wild goose chase."<ref name="Goosey" />
*'''Wild [[goose]] chase''' or '''wild-goose chase''': A futile search.<ref name="Star Wars (1977) 30" /><ref name="Trapped">''[[Rebel Force: Trapped]]''</ref> "Wild goose chase" is a real-world idiom.<ref name="Goosey" />
*'''[[Wild gundark chase]]''': See '''wild bantha chase'''.<ref name="DL" /><ref name="Honor Among Thieves" />
*'''Wild [[Mynock/Legends|mynock]] chase''': See '''wild bantha chase'''.<ref name="Game Chambers">''[[The Game Chambers of Questal]]''</ref><ref name="The Right Place">{{WEGCite|story=The Right Place ...|book=The Politics of Contraband}}</ref>
*'''Wild [[Yunax/Legends|yunax]] chase''': See '''wild bantha chase'''.<ref name="Hero's Trial">''[[The New Jedi Order: Agents of Chaos I: Hero's Trial]]''</ref>
*'''Wise-mouthed''': A term used by [[Jolli]] to describe [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], apparently referring to his tendency to make sarcastic remarks.<ref name="SW11" />
*'''Wishbone''': Slang term commonly used by [[Invids|Invid]] pilots, in reference to the [[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|BTL Y-wing starfighter]].<ref name="IJ" />
*'''With your tail in a sling''': A phrase used by [[Crimson Jack/Legends|Crimson Jack]], apparently meaning "being at a disadvantage" or "being in a bad situation."<ref name="SW11" /> Similar to the rude real-world idiom "(to have/get one's) ass in a sling," meaning (among other things) to be in deep trouble.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://idioms.thefreedictionary.com/get+(one%27s)+ass+in+a+sling|text=get (one's) ass in a sling|quote=''rude slang'' (...) '''ass in a sling, to have/get one's''' To be in deep trouble. |work=[[Wikipedia:The Free Dictionary|''The Free Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20250417214839}}</ref>
*'''Wizard''': Juvenile equivalent to "cool" (i.e. "that's so wizard, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Ani]]").<ref name="TPM" /> Also used as a derogatory term for [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] by individuals such as [[Owen Lars/Legends|Owen Lars]].<ref name="ANH" /> Real-world word for a man who practices sorcery; and informal adjective (mainly British) meaning "superb, outstanding."<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/wizard|text=wizard|quote=NOUN 1. a male witch or a man who practises or professes to practise magic or sorcery (...) ADJECTIVE 5. ''informal, mainly British'' superb; outstanding|work=[[Wikipedia:Collins English Dictionary|''Collins English Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20210507035200}}</ref>
*'''Wobbly kneed''': Scared, afraid; used by [[Deliah Blue]].<ref name="SWL2" />
*'''Woke up on the wrong side of the [[Starship/Legends|starship]]''': Having a bad [[Standard day/Legends|day]].<ref name="KOTOR" /> Similar to the real-world idiom "get up on the wrong side of the bed."<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/get-up-on-the-wrong-side-of-the-bed|text=get up on the wrong side of the bed|quote=to be in a bad mood and to be easily annoyed all day|work=[[Wikipedia:Cambridge University Press and Assessment|''Cambridge Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20220503093702}}</ref>
*'''Wokling''': A term for a baby [[Ewok/Legends|Ewok]].<ref name="EOV:C" />
*'''Won't be worth a pinch of [[moon dust]]''': Worthless.<ref name="The White Witch" /> Similar to the real-world idiom "not worth a hill of beans."<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://idioms.thefreedictionary.com/not+worth+a+hill+of+beans|text=not worth a hill of beans|quote=Of little or no importance, value, or worth.|work=[[Wikipedia:The Free Dictionary|''The Free Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20250417220322}}</ref>
*'''Wook''': Short for [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]].<ref name="AHF:GT" />
*'''Wookinate''': [[Deal-slang]] for rendering an enemy harmless by use of excessive force, like a Wookiee would do.<ref name="Gambler's Life" />
*'''Woosh''': Expletive used on [[Simpla-12]].<ref name="JA:TEE" />
*'''[[Worm/Legends|Worm]]''': A contemptible person.<ref name="Rogue Squadron 29" /><ref name="Empire 5">[[Empire 5|''Empire'' 5]]</ref> Real-world noun.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/worm|text=worm|quote=2 a: a human being who is an object of contempt, loathing, or pity|work=[[Wikipedia:Merriam-Webster|Merriam-Webster]]|archivedate=20230606235552}}</ref>
*'''Word port''': Slang for mouth, e.g. "Seal [[Booster Terrik|your]] word port, will you?"<ref name="Specter of the Past" />
*'''Worry-droid''': Slang term for a droid that worried too much.<ref name="SW9" />

==X==
==Y==
*'''Yaa-yaah''': [[The galaxy/Legends|The galaxy's]] most widespread greeting hailing from pre-[[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] times, and deemed insulting by [[Ugnaught/Legends|Ugnaughts]].<ref name="CSWE" />
*'''Yadaj dakl, ignot!''': A venomous [[Yuuzhan Vong]] curse.<ref name="NJOSB" />
*'''Yazbo''': A [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorrean]] derogatory word.<ref name="COTJ" />
*'''Yahoo!''': A battle cry used by [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]].<ref name="SW4" />
*'''You'll find my boot up your exhaust port''': Equivalent to "You'll find my boot up your rear end" or "I'll kick your ass."<ref name="SWL14">[[Legacy (2006) 14|''Legacy'' (2006) 14]]</ref>
*'''You're thermal''': A negative evaluation of a person's sanity. (The reply: "All musicians are thermal.")<ref name="We Don't Do Weddings: The Band's Tale">{{StoryCite|story=We Don't Do Weddings: The Band's Tale|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref>
*'''You-buh''' or '''UABH''': "Use a Bigger Hammer"; slang used by builders and mechanics.<ref name="DS" />
*'''[[Youngling/Legends|Youngling]]''': Another term for child, often used by the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi]].<ref name="TPM" /><ref name="AOTC" /><ref name="ROTS" />
*'''Yum-yum''': Slang term for lover or girlfriend.<ref name="Republic 81">[[Republic 81|''Republic'' 81]]</ref> Also used as an adjective to refer to someone physically attractive.<ref name="SW 20">[[Star Wars (1998) 20|''Star Wars'' (1998) 20]]</ref><ref name="SW43">[[Star Wars (1998) 43|''Star Wars'' (1998) 43]]</ref>

==Z==
*'''Zero Zero Zero''': Street slang for the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]],<ref name="RC:TZ" /> due to its [[Galactic coordinates/Legends|galactic coordinates]] being 0,0,0.<ref name="Zero Zero Zero">{{CSWECite|III|371|Zero Zero Zero}}</ref>
*'''Zones''': [[Gallisport]] [[Swoop gang/Legends|swoop gang]] slang. Territorial districts in Gallisport.<ref name="SG" />
*'''Zoomies''': Gallisport [[Swoop/Legends|swoop]] gang slang. Professional [[Swoop racing/Legends|swoop racers]].<ref name="SG" />
*'''Zot''': A curse word.<ref name="Rogue Squadron 3">[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron 3|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' 3]]</ref>
*'''Zyom''': A [[Human/Legends|Human]] expletive used by [[Debret Nightmoon]].<ref name="Buyer's Guide">{{Journal|5|A Buyer's Guide to Alternative Starships}}</ref>
